newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela can reach 30 pct inflation target--Casas.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela can reach 30 pct inflation target--Casas.

text.p: Venezuela is on track to reach its 30 percent year-end inflation target, Central Bank Governor Antonio Casas Gonzalez said Tuesday.

"If we get to the middle of the year with accumulated inflation of 15 percent, we can end with 30 percent ... people who say otherwise don't know what they're talking about. Inflation prospects look rather good," Casas told reporters after a conference.
Accumulated inflation for the first quarter stood at 9.1 percent, compared to 34.5 percent in the first quarter last year.
Low inflation will ensure positive interest rates by the end of the year, Casas added.
"The idea is for people to save and banks to intermediate (those savings); but for interest rates to be low, inflation has to be low as well," he said.
In its battle to mop up liquidity and fight inflation, Casas said the Central Bank would start using Treasury Bills in its open market operations within three weeks.
"They (the bills) should come to the market in three weeks ... alongside the Monetary Stabilization Notes (TEMs)," Casas said.

The long-awaited bills, approved last week, will be used to pay off the government's $3.7 billion debt with the Central Bank. Maturities will extend to 18 years, and the paper will carry interest equivalent to Libor plus 0.875 percentage point.
